headline: 7,500 Bangladeshis imprisoned in Saudi Arabia, says State Minister
summary: State Minister Shama Obaid Islam reveals the high number of prisoners and confirms the government is seeking details on two Bangladeshis facing the death penalty.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam announced that approximately 7,500 Bangladeshis are currently imprisoned in Saudi Arabia.

The Minister stated that the Bangladesh government has formally requested copies of the judgments for two Bangladeshis facing the death penalty in the Kingdom to understand the details of their cases.

These remarks were made at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, where the Minister was receiving the body of Md. Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi worker killed in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
The Minister noted that over 4 million Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia, making them vulnerable to regional conflicts and accidents.
In the last six months, the bodies of 11 Bangladeshis killed due to Middle East conflicts have been repatriated to Bangladesh.
The government is currently in discussions with Saudi Arabia regarding the extension of visas and iqamas for workers affected by these conflicts.
Regarding allegations of negligence by missions, the Minister emphasized that every mission has a labor welfare wing and any negligence will be investigated and addressed.
Md. Shahed Ahmed, a plumber from Bogura, was killed on October 10 during a Houthi attack at the Riyadh airport while returning to his workplace in Jeddah.
caption:
7,500 Bangladeshis are currently imprisoned in Saudi Arabia, and two are facing the death penalty.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam announced that approximately 7,500 Bangladeshis are currently imprisoned in Saudi Arabia.

The Minister stated that the Bangladesh government has formally requested copies of the judgments for two Bangladeshis facing the death penalty in the Kingdom to understand the details of their cases.

These remarks were made at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, where the Minister was receiving the body of Md. Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi worker killed in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.

The Minister noted that over 4 million Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia, making them vulnerable to regional conflicts and accidents.

In the last six months, the bodies of 11 Bangladeshis killed due to Middle East conflicts have been repatriated to Bangladesh.

The government is currently in discussions with Saudi Arabia regarding the extension of visas and iqamas for workers affected by these conflicts.

Regarding allegations of negligence by missions, the Minister emphasized that every mission has a labor welfare wing and any negligence will be investigated and addressed.

Md. Shahed Ahmed, a plumber from Bogura, was killed on October 10 during a Houthi attack at the Riyadh airport while returning to his workplace in Jeddah.

headline: Japan to arrange $6.35 billion in private investment for Bangladesh
summary: Japan plans to facilitate $6.35 billion in private investment in Bangladesh over the next five years, focusing on the automobile, manufacturing, and energy sectors. This significant economic cooperation is expected to be announced during Prime Minister Tareq R
details: Japan is set to arrange 1 trillion yen, equivalent to $6.35 billion, in private investment for Bangladesh within the next five years. The funds will be directed towards developing the automobile, manufacturing, and energy industries in the country.

This substantial investment initiative is anticipated to be formally announced during Prime Minister Tareq Rahman's upcoming visit to Tokyo, scheduled from October 26 to 29. A meeting between the prime ministers of both nations is planned for October 27.

According to a report by the Japanese newspaper Nikkei, this move signifies Japan's strategic intent to bolster its economic cooperation with Bangladesh, potentially as a counterbalance to China's growing influence in the region.

A delegation of Japanese business leaders is expected to visit Bangladesh soon. Discussions during this visit are planned to include a government-private sector dialogue focused on economic cooperation and investment opportunities.
caption:
Japan pledges $6.35 billion in private investment for Bangladesh's key sectors. The announcement is expected during PM Tareq Rahman's Tokyo visit.

Japan is set to arrange 1 trillion yen, equivalent to $6.35 billion, in private investment for Bangladesh within the next five years. The funds will be directed towards developing the automobile, manufacturing, and energy industries in the country.

This substantial investment initiative is anticipated to be formally announced during Prime Minister Tareq Rahman's upcoming visit to Tokyo, scheduled from October 26 to 29. A meeting between the prime ministers of both nations is planned for October 27.

According to a report by the Japanese newspaper Nikkei, this move signifies Japan's strategic intent to bolster its economic cooperation with Bangladesh, potentially as a counterbalance to China's growing influence in the region.

A delegation of Japanese business leaders is expected to visit Bangladesh soon. Discussions during this visit are planned to include a government-private sector dialogue focused on economic cooperation and investment opportunities.
